title: Named wave: save a set of items under a name and start it by name (state, daemon, CLI)
lead: *Proposed.* ork keeps a saved wave in a new ork state file next to the registry, keyed by project and name. `ork wave define NAME ITEM...`, `ork wave list`, `ork wave rm NAME` and `ork wave start NAME` manage and launch it. Run records carry the wave name. The Waves screen part is the next slice, `named-wave-tui`, which depends on this one.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner, 2026-10-31 (interactive questions on the v1.1 plan): group slices into a self-defined wave and run it by name; the wave is ork-side, stored in a new ork state file next to the registry and keyed by project and name; it is not stored in the project repo and needs no slicer change; the CLI and the Waves screen both use it; run records carry the wave name; done members show as done and are skipped on start. Of the three options the plan listed (a slicer `wave` field, reuse of a slicer flag or pass, an ork-side file), the owner chose the ork-side file.

Today a wave is only a runtime id. `newWaveID` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:588-592`) makes `wave-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxx` at `wave.start` and stamps it on each run record (`Wave`, `internal/runrec/record.go:261`; `docs/state.md:191`). `ork wave start PROJECT ITEM...` takes the item ids on every call (`wave.start-input`, adj 139: items). One wave is one project (`wave.scope`, adj 18). The Waves screen keeps its ticks only in memory (`picked` in `wavesState`, `internal/tui/waves.go:43`, dropped by `dropWaves`, `:77-82`), so the owner's choice is lost on exit.

Checked against slicer on 2026-10-31: slicer stores no wave. `slicer plan-parallel` only computes waves and "Does not lock, claim, start or write" (`../slicer/docs/commands.md:35`). `slicer --root ../slicer find wave` lists s376, s377, s392, s395 and s399, and none adds a stored wave field. `adj check "wave.named"` and `adj check "wave.name"` return `not found`: no record covers a saved wave yet. The decided wave keys that stay in force are `wave.start-input` (adj 139), `wave.scope` (adj 18), `wave.record` (adj 113: the wave id on the run record, queued state, caps in the daemon) and `wave.stop-target` (adj 138: `ork stop` tells a wave id from a run id by the `wave-` prefix).

Boundary (`docs/boundaries.md`, Ownership): the queue, items and wave suggestion are slicer's; ork owns "Registry, run records, fixtures, UI preferences". A saved wave holds only a name and item ids. It never stores item status, titles or specs: those are read from slicer on every use, so a member that finishes elsewhere shows as done without any write.

Split: this slice is the state file, the daemon methods, the run-record field and the CLI. The Waves screen (save the ticked set, launch by name) is `named-wave-tui`, which needs the daemon methods and `daemon.SavedWave.Startable` from this slice. Together they are more than one M Codex run, so they are two outlines.

Open owner questions (see MANIFEST-E.md, NW-Q1 to NW-Q6). The Implement steps name the question each default waits on. Do not start before the owner has answered NW-Q1 to NW-Q6; the implementer replaces each `[NW-Qn]` line with the answer.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
All paths below are *proposed*. This slice touches `internal/daemon` and `internal/engine`: it is an E-class slice (design.md, Self-hosting: at most one such slice per wave).

- `internal/wavestore/wavestore.go` (new): the file type, Load, Save, name validation, atomic write.
- `internal/wavestore/wavestore_test.go` (new).
- `internal/daemon/waves.go` (new): wave.define, wave.list, wave.rm handlers, the SavedWave types and Startable.
- `internal/daemon/waves_test.go` (new).
- `internal/daemon/wire.go:21-27` (the MethodWave* constants; the params and result types live in `internal/daemon/waves.go`).
- `internal/daemon/handlers.go:83-107` (dispatch; registryPath at :28 gives the directory of the new file) and `internal/daemon/handlers.go:526-555` (removeProject, for NW-Q6).
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` (the new `waveMu` field beside `regMu`).
- `internal/daemon/client.go:324-356` (client methods beside WaveStart).
- `internal/daemon/runs.go:1089-1230` (WaveStartParams gains Name; WaveResult gains Name; startWave validates and stamps it), `internal/daemon/runs.go:800` (admitRun passes it to the engine config) and the unexported `waveName` field of RunParams.
- `internal/engine/engine.go:107-119` (Config.WaveName) and :380 (the record it creates).
- `internal/engine/resume.go:55-65` and :142 (WithWaveName: a start that resumes a stopped run sets wave_name beside wave).
- `internal/runrec/record.go:311` (WaveName beside Wave).
- `internal/runrec/runrec_test.go`, `internal/engine/engine_test.go`, `internal/engine/stoppedresume_test.go`.
- `internal/daemon/runs_test.go` (newWaveRigRoutes) and `internal/daemon/stoppedresume_test.go` (the autoResumeLocked call and the resumed-run name test).
- `internal/slicercli/slicercli.go:49-66` (a ListAll method that runs slicer list --all --json --lean --root ROOT; List omits done and retired items) and its test in `internal/slicercli/slicercli_test.go`.
- `internal/cli/wave.go:19-310` (dispatch, the new define, list and rm commands, and waveStart split into waveStart and startWave so a saved wave and a typed item list share one path).
- `internal/cli/cli.go:68-85` (usage text) and `internal/cli/wave_test.go` (TestWaveUsage at :266 becomes TestWaveUsageListsDefineListRmStart).
- `docs/state.md` (the "What ork owns" table at :8-23, a new `waves.json` section before `## run.json`, wave_name in the run.json example and notes), `docs/design.md:108-115` (method table), :1727-1735 (CLI list) and the Wave lifecycle (:171-195), `docs/guide.md` section 9 (:417-), `docs/boundaries.md` (Ownership table row for saved waves), `docs/glossary.md:225-232` (the ork Wave entry gains "named wave"; :175 is slicer's wave and stays), `README.md` wave paragraph.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (an entry under ## Unreleased, marked *proposed*).

Pair planning: E-class. Do not put it in a wave with another slice that touches `internal/engine`, `internal/daemon` or cmd. It can pair with an N-class slice that avoids `internal/cli/wave.go`, `docs/design.md` and `docs/state.md`, for example the docs re-anchor slice only if that one runs after this one (both edit `docs/design.md` and `docs/guide.md`). named-wave-tui must come after it.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Each test is named, with the reason it fails before the change.

`internal/wavestore/wavestore_test.go` (the package does not exist, so every test fails to compile first):
- `TestLoadMissingFileIsEmptyAndCreatesNothing`: a missing file loads as empty and no file or directory is made.
- `TestSaveLoadRoundTripKeepsOrder`: waves and items come back in the order saved.
- `TestSameNameInTwoProjectsAreTwoWaves`: the key is project plus name.
- `TestPutDuplicateNeedsReplaceAndKeepsPositionAndCreatedAt`: a replace keeps the wave's place and created_at.
- `TestLoadRefusesUnknownKeysAndNewerVersion`: strict keys, as `registry.Load` does.
- `TestSaveIsAtomicAndWritesTheModeFromNWQ5`: temporary file in the same directory, then rename; the mode is the one the owner picked in NW-Q5 (0600); a write failure leaves the old file and no temporary file.
- `TestNameRulesFromNWQ2`: table test of accepted and refused names and item counts.

`internal/daemon/waves_test.go` (methods do not exist: `unknown_method`):
- `TestWaveDefineStoresNameAndItemsInOrder`: result has project, name, items, `created_at`; the file sits in the registry's directory.
- `TestWaveDefineDuplicateNameFollowsNWQ3`: refuse with `duplicate_name` unless `replace`.
- `TestWaveDefineItemRulesFollowNWQ4`: an unknown item id at define time, and a repeated item id, behave as NW-Q4 and NW-Q2 say.
- `TestWaveDefineUnknownProjectIsNotFound`: `not_found` with the registry guide text, as `registered` does.
- `TestWaveListReadsStatusFromSlicerWithOneListPerProject`: members carry `status` and `title` from a single faked `slicer list --all`; a member absent from that list has status `missing`; the fake records one list call per project, not one per member.
- `TestWaveListReportsASlicerErrorOnThatProjectsWavesOnly`: a slicer error for one project is an `error` on its waves and the other projects still list.
- `TestWaveListFiltersByProject`.
- `TestWaveRmRemovesOnlyThatProjectsWave` and `TestWaveRmUnknownIsNotFound`.
- `TestSavedWaveStartableSkipsDoneRetiredAndMissing`: `Startable` returns the members whose status is neither `done` nor `retired` nor `missing` (the NW-Q4 answer for start time), in saved order, plus the skipped members with their status.
- `TestWaveStartWithNameStampsWaveNameOnEveryRun`: every admitted run record has `WaveName` set and the same `Wave` id; the result carries `name`.
- `TestWaveStartWithoutNameLeavesWaveNameEmpty`: existing callers are unchanged (the existing `TestWaveStartStampsOneWaveIDOnEachRun` still passes).
- `TestWaveStartNameMustBeSavedAndItemsMustBeMembers`: an unsaved name is `not_found`; an item that is not a member is `bad_params`; nothing is admitted in either case.
- `TestRemoveProjectKeepsOrDropsSavedWavesPerNWQ6`: `projects rm` drops the project's saved waves (a refused removal keeps them).
- `TestWaveMethodsRefuseConcurrentWritersCleanly`: concurrent defines and rms all end in a valid file (one lock, as `regMu` serialises registry writes).

`internal/daemon/stoppedresume_test.go`: `TestWaveStartResumedRunJoinsTheNewWaveName` (a start that resumes a stopped run sets its wave_name, and clears an older one for an unnamed wave).

`internal/runrec/runrec_test.go`: `TestRecordWaveNameRoundTrips` and `TestRecordWithoutWaveNameStillLoads` (field unknown, so strict decode fails first).

`internal/engine/engine_test.go`: `TestEngineRecordsWaveName` (Config has no `WaveName`). `internal/engine/stoppedresume_test.go`: `TestResumeJoinsTheWaveNameOfTheCaller` (`WithWaveName` does not exist).

`internal/slicercli`: `TestListAllPassesAllFlag` (no `ListAll`; the fake `slicer` route expects `list --all --json --lean --root ROOT`).

`internal/cli/wave_test.go`:
- `TestWaveDefineListRm`: define prints the saved wave; list prints name, project, and each member with its status; `--json` shapes; rm removes it.
- `TestWaveStartByNameSkipsDoneMembers`: with one member `done`, the plan, spec check and `wave.start` calls cover only the others; the output names the skipped member and its status; `WaveStartParams.Name` is the saved name.
- `TestWaveStartByNameWithNoStartableMemberDoesNotStart`: prints `no item is ready to start` style text, exit 1, no `wave.start` call; `--json` has `started:false`, `held:[]` and `skipped`.
- `TestWaveStartByNameUnknownNameIsNotFound`.
- `TestWaveStartByNameKeepsTheTypedFormWorking`: `ork wave start P A B` still starts a wave with no name.
- `TestWaveStartByNameAppliesFlagsToEveryMember`: `--yes`, `--well-specified`, `--split`, lineup flags and `--stop-after` behave as for a typed list.
- `TestWaveUsageListsDefineListRmStart` (replaces the text in `TestWaveUsage`).
- `TestWaveProjectArgumentFollowsNWQ1`: the project argument form NW-Q1 picked, including the ambiguous-name case.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Write the failing tests first, in the order above. Do not touch: `internal/tui` (that is `named-wave-tui`), `internal/engine/land.go`, the registry file format (`internal/registry` keeps its version and strict keys; saved waves are a separate file), `ork stop` (it keeps taking a `wave-` id; a name is not accepted there), and slicer data (no `slicer set`, `--flag` or `--pass` writes).

1. Preflight. The owner must have answered NW-Q1 to NW-Q6 in MANIFEST-E.md. Replace each `[NW-Qn]` below with the answer and cite "owner, DATE". If any is unanswered, stop and report; do not choose.
2. `internal/wavestore` (*proposed* package). File `waves.json` in the registry's directory (`filepath.Dir(registry path)`), name and mode per `[NW-Q5]`. Shape (version 1, strict keys, like `projects.json`):
   `{"version":1,"waves":[{"project":"ork","name":"pair-a","items":["S50","S69"],"created_at":"...","updated_at":"..."}]}`.
   `Load` returns an empty file for a missing path and creates nothing. `Save` writes a temporary file in the same directory, syncs, renames (copy the pattern of `registry.Save`, `internal/registry/registry.go:349-392`). Name and item rules per `[NW-Q2]`. Duplicate name per `[NW-Q3]`.
3. `internal/slicercli`: add `ListAll` next to `List`.
4. Daemon: types and handlers in `internal/daemon/waves.go`; constants in `wire.go` (`wave.define`, `wave.list`, `wave.rm`, all *proposed wire*); dispatch in `handlers.go`; client methods in `client.go`. Writes take a new mutex (`waveMu`) so two writers never interleave; do not reuse `regMu`, which guards `projects.json`.
   - `wave.define` params `{project,name,items,replace?}`; result the saved wave. The project must be registered (`d.registered`). Item checks per `[NW-Q4]`, read through `ListAll`.
   - `wave.list` params `{project?}`; result `{waves:[{project,name,items:[{item,status,title}],created_at,updated_at}]}`. Status comes from one `ListAll` per project; an item not in that list has status `missing`. A slicer error for a project is returned as an `error` on that project's waves, not as a failure of the whole call (other projects still list).
   - `wave.rm` params `{project,name}`; `not_found` when absent.
   - Export `func (w SavedWaveView) Startable() (ids []string, skipped []SkippedItem)` so the CLI and the TUI use one rule. `[NW-Q4]` decides what is skipped at start; the default tests above assume done, retired and missing are skipped and named, and nothing is written back to the file.
   - `removeProject` (`handlers.go:479-508`): `[NW-Q6]`.
5. `wave.start`: `WaveStartParams` gains optional `Name string json:"name,omitempty"`. When set, `startWave` requires a saved wave of that name for the project (else `not_found`) and every item to be a member (else `bad_params`), before it reads dependencies or admits anything. It stamps the name into `engine.Config.WaveName` (new), and `engine.New` writes it to `runrec.Record.WaveName` (`json:"wave_name,omitempty"`, additive; the record version stays 1; an older ork refuses a record that has it because `Store.Open` uses strict keys, as `docs/state.md` says for `dismissed_at`). `WaveResult` gains `Name`. The wave id stays a fresh `newWaveID` on every start; the name is a label, not an id.
6. CLI (`internal/cli/wave.go`): add `define`, `list` and `rm`; the project argument form per `[NW-Q1]`. Split `waveStart` so the part after "resolve project and item list" is shared: `ork wave start NAME` reads the saved wave with `wave.list`, takes `Startable()`, prints each skipped member and its status on stderr in JSON mode and on stdout otherwise, then plans, spec-checks, confirms and starts as today, with `Name` set. One positional argument to `wave start` is a name; two or more stay `PROJECT ITEM...` (one positional is a usage error today, `internal/cli/wave.go:100-102`, so nothing changes for existing use). A wave with no startable member exits 1 with no `wave.start` call. `ork wave list` text: one block per wave, `NAME  PROJECT` then `  ITEM  STATUS  TITLE` lines; `--json` prints the daemon result.
7. Docs, all marked *proposed*: `docs/state.md` (file, shape, mode, `wave_name`), `docs/design.md` (three methods, `name` on `wave.start`, CLI list, a sentence in the Wave lifecycle that a wave may be named), `docs/guide.md` section 9 (define, list, start by name, rm), `docs/boundaries.md` (ork owns saved waves: names and item ids only), `docs/glossary.md`, `README.md`.
8. CHANGELOG entry last, as the final edit, under `## Unreleased`, one paragraph starting `Named wave (*proposed*):`. Add it after everything else so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict.

UI slice: UI pass (r14). It changes `internal/cli` output.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). NW-Q1 to NW-Q9 as drafted in this spec: --project P; a name is 1 to 32 characters of [a-z0-9._-]; refuse a duplicate name unless --replace; refuse unknown items at define time and skip done or retired items at start; waves.json is mode 0600; drop a project's saved waves on 'projects rm'; no wave name in the TUI for now.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/wavestore ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli ./internal/runrec ./internal/engine ./internal/slicercli`.
- `rg -n "waves.json" docs/state.md docs/design.md docs/guide.md` shows the same file name in all three.
- `rg -n "Co-Authored|Generated" CHANGELOG.md` shows nothing new.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] After the owner rebuilds and restarts the daemon (`ork daemon restart`, which refuses while a role runs), run `ork wave define --help`-style usage, define a wave of two open items, `ork wave list` (members show their status; a done item shows done), and `ork wave rm` it. Do not start a real wave for this check. Confirm the file exists beside `projects.json` with the agreed mode.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Named wave: saved waves in a state file, wave define, list, rm and start by name".
